name: yutu

hlido_opinion.headline: A genuinely tri-modal YouTube toolkit — CLI, MCP server and A2A agent from one binary — whose install path is verifiable and whose 'autopilot' claim is not.
hlido_opinion.body: yutu is unusual in this crop for shipping three interfaces over one codebase: a 30+ command CLI, an MCP server you drop into Claude Desktop, Cursor or OpenCode, and an A2A agent mode. The public surface backs the mechanical claims well — brew, winget and a curl installer are all published, the MCP config snippet is copy-pasteable, and the resource list (video, playlist, caption, thumbnail, membership, super-chat, i18n, abuse report) reads like it was generated from the YouTube Data API surface rather than from a marketing brainstorm. Apache-2.0 with the repo linked from the fold. Where it thins out is exactly where the headline promise lives. 'Grows your YouTube channel on autopilot' and 'autonomous multi-agent system' are the two load-bearing claims, and neither is evidenced anywhere on the public surface — no demo of the agent running, no description of what the agents decide, no before/after. What is demonstrably shipped is comprehensive YouTube API automation, which is a useful and honest product; the autonomy layer on top is asserted. For a buyer, the CLI and MCP surface is the part to evaluate on, and it is strong. Treat the agent mode as unproven until you run it.

tier_rationale: STEADY because the verifiable core — a broad, well-organised YouTube automation surface exposed through three interfaces with real install paths and an OSI licence — is solid and immediately usable. Held below the top band because the product's own headline claim (autonomous channel growth) has no public evidence behind it, and because there is no demo or docs surface deep enough to check what the agent mode actually does.
what_it_does_well: Three interfaces (CLI, MCP server, A2A agent) from a single install — rare and genuinely useful
Install paths published for macOS, Windows and Linux, all copy-pasteable
MCP config snippet given verbatim, with named clients (Claude Desktop, OpenCode, Cursor)
Resource coverage is broad and specific — 20+ YouTube entity types enumerated, not hand-waved
Apache-2.0, repo linked prominently from the landing page
what_it_fails_at: 'Autopilot' / 'autonomous multi-agent system' is asserted with zero public evidence — no demo, no decision description
No documentation surface beyond the landing page; the four-step quickstart is the whole story
No description of how OAuth credentials are stored or scoped, despite the tool requiring full channel write access
No changelog, roadmap or release cadence signal on the public surface
The A2A agent invocation is shown as a bare flag string with no explanation of the modes it takes
best_for: Creators and channel operators who want scriptable YouTube automation and are comfortable in a terminal
Developers wiring YouTube management into an AI editor over MCP
Teams replacing brittle hand-rolled YouTube Data API scripts with a maintained CLI
CI/CD publishing pipelines (GitHub Actions and Docker are both named)
not_recommended_for: Buyers who need the autonomous growth claim to be real before committing — it is unevidenced
Non-technical creators; every documented path starts at a shell prompt
Anyone needing a documented data-handling or credential-storage posture before granting channel write access
red_flags: The headline promise ('grows your YouTube channel on autopilot') is the single least-evidenced thing on the page, which inverts the usual expectation that the biggest claim carries the most proof.
The tool requires OAuth credentials with broad YouTube write scope, and the public surface says nothing about how those credentials are handled.

compared_to.verdict_diff: n8n is the general-purpose automation platform with a YouTube node among hundreds; yutu is YouTube-only but far deeper on that one API. Choose n8n if YouTube is one step in a wider workflow, yutu if YouTube IS the workflow.
Zapier is no-code and hosted; yutu is a self-hosted binary you authenticate yourself. Zapier wins on accessibility, yutu on API coverage and cost (free).

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: First-class MCP server with a published stdio config, plus an A2A agent mode. An agent can drive the full YouTube entity surface through named tools. The CLI is equally scriptable. This is one of the more agent-addressable tools in its category — the limiting factor is credential setup, not interface availability.

claims.claim: Homepage publicly accessible and value proposition clearly stated
claims.evidence: Landing page loads without auth; states 'CLI · MCP Server · AI Agent — Automate your entire YouTube workflow' above the fold.

claims.claim: Pricing page discoverable in 2 clicks from homepage
claims.evidence: No pricing surface exists. The tool is Apache-2.0 and distributed free via package managers, so a pricing page is not expected; absence is not a defect here.

claims.claim: Documentation or live demo accessible without login
claims.evidence: A four-step quickstart with real install and config commands is public, but there is no separate docs site or live demo. Enough to install, not enough to evaluate the agent mode.

claims.claim: Integration list or supported frameworks documented
claims.evidence: Named integrations published: Claude Desktop, OpenCode, Cursor, GitHub Actions, Docker, A2A, plus an OpenClaw skill.

claims.claim: Authentication / data handling claims publicly stated
claims.evidence: The auth step is shown ('yutu auth --credential client_secret.json') but no statement covers how credentials are stored, scoped or revoked.

evidence_urls.claim: Homepage publicly accessible and value proposition clearly stated
Pricing page discoverable in 2 clicks from homepage
Documentation or live demo accessible without login
Integration list or supported frameworks documented
Authentication / data handling claims publicly stated

marking_signal.rationale: Automation and publishing toolkit for an existing video platform; it does not itself generate synthetic media, so Article 50(4) marking duties do not attach to its output.

pricing_facts.basis: Derived from Hlido-held evidence only (engine checklist + editorial text); quotes are verbatim from the scorecard; not vendor-supplied; re-derived daily. Verify current prices on the vendor's pricing page.
